headline: Highest risk is prompt-injection and cascading-error from Cline parsing untrusted prompt-leak content; data leakage and compliance risks are lower but present.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cline can read workspace files, use MCP, and run browsers, so it may ingest attacker-controlled content; system_prompts_leaks is explicitly about leaked prompts and could supply malicious instructions. The pairwise pathway is plausible, but B has no execution surface, so the risk is mediated through Cline alone.
conditions: IF Cline reads content from a shared workspace or MCP source that contains adversarial instructions, THEN prompt injection is possible.
IF system_prompts_leaks content is copied into Cline's browser or file inputs, THEN Cline may follow embedded instructions.
mitigations: Disable MCP sources not needed for the task.
Keep system_prompts_leaks content out of shared workspaces.
Use a separate read-only folder for untrusted text.
Require manual review before any tool action triggered by file content.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cline touches source code and browser screenshots and has broad network egress, while system_prompts_leaks is source-available and non-runnable with no data classes listed. There is no documented shared sensitive dataset, so leakage is limited to accidental exposure of code or screenshots if the pair shares files.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace containing secrets, THEN Cline can exfiltrate those files over the network.
IF browser screenshots include sensitive content and are copied into shared files, THEN they may be exposed.
mitigations: Store secrets outside the shared workspace.
Run Cline in a separate project folder.
Review outbound network destinations before use.
Delete screenshots after task completion.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level access controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cline has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and shared_state_with_other_instances via filesystem; system_prompts_leaks has no write or concurrency fields, so direct conflict is one-sided but still plausible if both touch the same repo or workspace. Uncertainty about B's operational surface pushes this above low.
conditions: IF system_prompts_leaks is wrapped in a workflow that writes to the same repository as Cline, THEN file and git conflicts can occur.
IF both agents operate on the same workspace concurrently, THEN Cline may overwrite B-produced artifacts.
mitigations: Assign separate workspaces.
Pause one agent before the other writes.
Use git branches per agent.
Check for uncommitted changes before each write.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared filesystem state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cline can generate code or browser-derived outputs that another agent could treat as authoritative, and system_prompts_leaks is a prompt-leak corpus that may be used as reference material without verification. The pair lacks a built-in verification step, so errors can cascade if B consumes Cline's outputs or vice versa.
conditions: IF system_prompts_leaks is used to summarize or transform Cline-produced artifacts, THEN unverified errors can propagate.
IF Cline ingests text from system_prompts_leaks as factual guidance, THEN downstream actions may be based on false premises.
mitigations: Require a human check before acting on generated facts.
Cross-check outputs against primary sources.
Separate drafting from execution roles.
Mark unverified content clearly in filenames.
requires-engineering: add validation gates before any action-taking step.

E_compliance.rationale: Cline handles source code and browser screenshots with broad egress, while system_prompts_leaks is source-available and not runnable; no explicit residency or regulated-data mismatch is documented. The only plausible compliance issue is accidental handling of sensitive code or screenshots in Cline, so the pairwise compliance risk is limited.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Cline's workspace, THEN its network egress may create a compliance issue.
IF screenshots contain personal data and are retained in shared storage, THEN retention policy mismatches can arise.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in the shared workspace.
Review retention settings for screenshots.
Use redacted test data.
Document data-handling boundaries.
requires-engineering: implement residency and retention controls.
